3D scatter plots

Source: R/geom-point-3d.R
geom_point_3d.Rd

geom_point_3d() creates scatter plots in 3D space with automatic depth-based size scaling. Points closer to the viewer appear larger, while points farther away appear smaller, creating realistic perspective effects.

Usage

geom_point_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = StatPoint3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  annotate = deprecated(),
  na.rm = FALSE,
  sort_method = deprecated(),
  scale_depth = TRUE,
  on_top = FALSE,
  flat = FALSE,
  raw_points = deprecated(),
  ref_lines = deprecated(),
  ref_points = deprecated(),
  ref_faces = deprecated(),
  ref_circle_radius = deprecated(),
  ref_circle_vertices = deprecated(),
  ref_line_color = deprecated(),
  ref_line_colour = deprecated(),
  ref_line_linewidth = deprecated(),
  ref_line_linetype = deprecated(),
  ref_line_alpha = deprecated(),
  ref_point_color = deprecated(),
  ref_point_colour = deprecated(),
  ref_point_fill = deprecated(),
  ref_point_size = deprecated(),
  ref_point_alpha = deprecated(),
  ref_point_stroke = deprecated(),
  ref_point_shape = deprecated(),
  inherit.aes = TRUE,
  show.legend = NA
)

stat_point_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomPoint3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  sort_method = deprecated(),
  scale_depth = TRUE,
  raw_points = deprecated(),
  ref_lines = deprecated(),
  ref_points = deprecated(),
  ref_faces = deprecated(),
  ref_circle_radius = deprecated(),
  ref_circle_vertices = deprecated(),
  ref_line_color = deprecated(),
  ref_line_colour = deprecated(),
  ref_line_linewidth = deprecated(),
  ref_line_linetype = deprecated(),
  ref_line_alpha = deprecated(),
  ref_point_color = deprecated(),
  ref_point_colour = deprecated(),
  ref_point_fill = deprecated(),
  ref_point_size = deprecated(),
  ref_point_alpha = deprecated(),
  ref_point_stroke = deprecated(),
  ref_point_shape = deprecated(),
  inherit.aes = TRUE,
  show.legend = NA
)

Arguments

mapping

Set of aesthetic mappings created by aes(). In addition to the standard point aesthetics, geom_point_3d() requires x, y, and z coordinates.

data

The data to be displayed in this layer.

stat

The statistical transformation to use on the data. Defaults to "point_3d".

position

Position adjustment, defaults to "identity". Use position_on_face() to place points on faces of the panel.

...

Other arguments passed on to ggplot2::layer().

annotate

Deprecated. Add annotations to the plot with + annotate_3d() instead. All 3D layers in a panel are depth-sorted together, so annotations no longer need to be embedded in a layer.

na.rm

If FALSE, missing values are removed with a warning.

sort_method

Deprecated. All 3D layers in a panel are now depth-sorted together, pairwise, so this has no effect. See sorting_methods.

scale_depth

Controls depth-based scaling, drawing closer elements larger or thicker and farther ones smaller or thinner. TRUE (the default) applies full scaling and FALSE disables it; a number sets the strength directly, where 1 matches TRUE, 0 matches FALSE, values below 1 subdue the effect and values above 1 exaggerate it. This affects the layer only; use coord_3d(scale_depth = ) for panel and axis components.

on_top

If TRUE, the layer is drawn on top of the rest of the scene instead of being depth-sorted with it, so other geometry never hides or cuts it, e.g. to keep labels legible. The layers drawn on top are depth-sorted among themselves. Default FALSE.

flat

If TRUE, points placed on a face of the panel by position_on_face() are drawn as markers lying flat in that face, like shadows, rather than as symbols facing the viewer. Flat markers match the size of ordinary markers at the centre of the panel, and are drawn in true perspective, outlines included, whatever scale_depth is. They can be open, solid, or filled circles, squares, diamonds, or triangles (shapes 0, 1, 2, 5, 6, and 15 to 25). Points not on a face (e.g. with position_on_face(c("3D", "zmin"))) are drawn as usual. Default FALSE.

raw_points, ref_lines, ref_points, ref_faces, ref_circle_radius, ref_circle_vertices

Deprecated. Reference elements are now drawn by separate layers: drop lines by geom_dropline_3d(), and reference points by geom_point_3d() with position = position_on_face() (and flat = TRUE for circles).

ref_line_color, ref_line_colour, ref_line_linewidth, ref_line_linetype, ref_line_alpha

Deprecated. Style a geom_dropline_3d() layer instead.

ref_point_color, ref_point_colour, ref_point_fill, ref_point_size, ref_point_alpha, ref_point_stroke, ref_point_shape

Deprecated. Style a geom_point_3d(position = position_on_face()) layer instead.

inherit.aes

If FALSE, overrides the default aesthetics.

show.legend

Logical indicating whether this layer should be included in legends.

geom

The geometric object used to display the data. Defaults to "point_3d".

Value

A Layer object that can be added to a ggplot.

Details

StatPoint3D performs identity transformation (passes data through unchanged) while properly handling discrete scales for 3D coordinate systems.

Aesthetics

geom_point_3d() supports all the same aesthetics as ggplot2::geom_point(), plus z:

  • x: X coordinate (required)

  • y: Y coordinate (required)

  • z: Z coordinate (required)

  • alpha: Transparency

  • colour: Point border color

  • fill: Point fill color (for certain shapes)

  • shape: Point shape

  • size: Point size (gets depth-scaled when scale_depth = TRUE)

  • stroke: Border width for shapes with borders

StatPoint3D returns the following computed variables

  • x_raw, y_raw, z_raw: Original values before discrete-to-numeric conversion

Depth Scaling

The depth scaling uses an inverse relationship with distance, following the mathematical relationship: apparent_size = base_size * reference_distance / actual_distance

This creates realistic perspective where:

  • Objects twice as far appear half as big

  • Objects twice as close appear twice as big

  • The center of the plot volume renders at exactly the user-specified size

Point Rendering

ggcube uses shape-aware rendering for improved stroke behavior:

  • Simple shapes (0-20, characters): Use size for fontsize, stroke for border width, no fill

  • Complex shapes (21-25): Use ggplot2's approach: size + 0.5*stroke for fontsize to prevent gaps

  • Both size and stroke are depth-scaled when scale_depth = TRUE

  • All shapes preserve stroke depth scaling and parameter control

Reference elements

To show where points lie in 3D, combine a point layer with layers that project the points onto faces of the panel:

  • geom_dropline_3d() draws lines from the points to faces.

  • geom_point_3d(position = position_on_face()) draws the points on faces, as upright markers, or with flat = TRUE, as markers lying in the faces.

All of these layers are depth-sorted together.

See also

geom_dropline_3d() for drop lines, position_on_face() for placing points on faces, geom_segment_3d() for 3D segments, geom_path_3d() for 3D paths, coord_3d() for 3D coordinate systems.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

# Basic 3D scatter plot with depth scaling
ggplot(expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:5, z = 1:5),
       aes(x, y, z, fill = z)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 10, shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = .1) +
  coord_3d(pitch = 40, roll = 5, yaw = 0, dist = 1.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c()


# Points with flat markers on two faces, and drop lines to them
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, qsec)) +
  geom_dropline_3d(faces = c("ymax", "xmax")) +
  geom_point_3d(position = position_on_face(c("ymax", "xmax")),
                flat = TRUE, alpha = .5, size = 3) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  coord_3d()


# Points and their shadows on the floor, in one layer
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, qsec, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point_3d(position = position_on_face(c("3D", "zmin")), flat = TRUE,
                shape = 21, size = 3) +
  coord_3d()
